task.description: RE-VALIDATION (rework attempt 2 of 3, last before mandatory ORCH escalation) of TEST-DESIGNER's claimed fix (commit 6dde119) to the same AC3 defect blocked twice already: attempt 0 hardcoded pre-call count 0 (fails 2nd+ invocation); attempt 1 captured a count_before baseline without resetting first (still fails 2nd+ invocation, because the un-reset baseline was itself already polluted). Claimed fix this round: reset_subject_row!/2 does a Repo.delete_all scoped identically to user_count_for_subject/2, called BEFORE any baseline count is read, intended to make the 0 -> 1 -> 1 sequence hold on every invocation. Independently verify: (a) reset runs strictly before the first count read in actual statement order; (b) delete query scope is provably identical to the count query's scope (tenant schema/prefix, realm, external_id) so it cannot touch any row outside this fixture identity; (c) delete_all is synchronous, no race; (d) the 0->1->1 sequence is structurally guaranteed on any invocation including a zero-match delete_all no-op; (e) the fixture row is exclusively test data, not real tenant data; (f) test/specs/REQ-134.md's AC3 section matches the final code with no stale narrative; (g) full re-check of every other Step 3b criterion (all 6 ACs covered, no TODOs, no unresolved @tag :skip, fixture isolation, self-sufficiency, no hardcoded secrets).
acceptance_criteria: a test obtains a genuine token from the running Keycloak and drives it through Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline end to end, with the real assertion output quoted
the token's signature is verified against the live JWKS via the real verifier, not TokenVerifierDouble -- demonstrated by the test failing if pointed at a tampered token
JIT provisioning creates a real user row on first authentication and reuses it on the second, asserted across two calls
the default mix test run still passes with Keycloak stopped, quoted as evidence
the real-token tests skip with a message naming exactly what must be running, rather than failing obscurely
the result states the exact command a developer runs to execute them

result.summary:
Checked out feature/WF02-REQ134-20260823 at commit 6dde119 (git pull confirmed up to date). Read handoff history first for context only, then independently re-read test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs, test/specs/REQ-134.md, test/support/keycloak_test_client.ex, and test/test_helper.exs in full from disk, not trusting either prior narrative.

AC3 reset-then-baseline logic, verified statement-by-statement (lines 259-298): the test obtains a real designer-user token, derives `subject = jwt_subject(raw_token)` (line 269), then on line 282 calls `reset_subject_row!(schema_name, subject)` BEFORE the first count read at line 284 (`assert user_count_for_subject(schema_name, subject) == 0`). This is strict program order in a single synchronous ExUnit test process -- there is no way for the count read to execute before the reset call above it. reset_subject_row!/2 (lines 199-205) is `User |> where([u], u.external_realm == @realm and u.external_id == ^subject) |> Repo.delete_all(prefix: schema_name)`. user_count_for_subject/2 (lines 183-187) is `User |> where([u], u.external_realm == @realm and u.external_id == ^subject) |> Repo.aggregate(:count, :id, prefix: schema_name)`. Both build from the identical `where` clause (same @realm module attribute, same `subject` variable, both filtering only `external_realm` and `external_id`) and the identical `prefix: schema_name` option -- not two independently-typed queries that could drift, but two call sites sharing the same filter shape verbatim in the same file, checked by hand for any typo/asymmetry (none found: same field names, same operator, same binding order). schema_name comes from `TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant(tenant.id)` for the bpm-default tenant specifically (ensure_bpm_default_tenant!/0, lines 127-154) -- confirmed this is bpm-default's own physical Postgres schema, not a shared/broader scope; per REQ-063 schema-per-tenant (restated correctly in both the test's own comment at lines 189-198 and REQ-134.md lines 98-104), there is no tenant_id column and no cross-schema query possible from this call at all, so the delete is structurally incapable of reaching another tenant. Repo.delete_all is synchronous (no Task.async/spawn anywhere in the file, confirmed by reading the whole module) so there is no race between the reset and the subsequent count read. Ecto's Repo.delete_all on a query matching zero rows is a standard no-op returning `{0, nil}` and raises nothing -- the code at line 202-204 does not pattern-match or branch on the return value at all (just calls it and returns `:ok`), so a zero-match first-ever-run case behaves identically to a non-zero-match repeat-run case: both leave the row deleted (or already-absent) with the function returning :ok either way. This means the 0 -> 1 -> 1 sequence is now structurally guaranteed on every invocation, not just a fresh database: reset always leaves count 0 (line 284's assert==0 confirms this is asserted, not merely assumed), call 1 (line 286) drives a genuine first-time provision every time (real find-or-create finds nothing because the row was just deleted), count goes to 1 (line 290), call 2 (line 292) hits the reuse branch of provision_oidc_user/4's upsert (same subject, row now exists), count stays 1 (line 297), and user_id_1 == user_id_2 (line 296) proves it is literally the same row reused, not a delete-and-reinsert coincidence. The designer-user row is exclusively test-fixture data: a JIT-provisioned row keyed to a fixed seeded Keycloak dev credential (designer-user/designer-pass, already vetted against REQ-128's known dev-only seed in the prior gate iterations, re-confirmed present in this file with no other consumer), owned entirely by this test's own lifecycle -- the reset cannot touch real application data because nothing outside this fixture identity shares (external_realm='bpm-default', external_id=<designer-user's fixed sub>) in this schema.

test/specs/REQ-134.md AC3 section (lines 90-140) matches the final code exactly: describes the reset-then-baseline mechanism, the identical-scope justification, the schema-per-tenant safety argument, and an accurate three-attempt history (rework 0 hardcoded-0, rework 1 un-reset baseline diff, rework 2 this reset-first version) with no stale claims about either superseded approach being current.

Full re-check of remaining Step 3b criteria: (a) AC1 (lines 211-229), AC2 (235-252), AC3 (258-299) each have >=1 runnable test; AC4 mechanism is test/test_helper.exs's exclude tag, AC5 is the setup_all raise with the documented deviation, AC6 is the moduledoc's stated command -- all present and unchanged from prior passes, re-read fresh this round, no regressions found. (b) No 'TODO: implement test' anywhere in the four files (grepped). (c) No `@tag :skip` anywhere (grepped; the only hits for 'skip' are prose/comments describing the documented {:skip,...}-vs-raise deviation, not an actual skip tag) -- and this is a MUST-covering module with no skip in play at all, so the paired-passing-counterpart clause is moot. (d) Fixtures: AC1/AC2 use admin-user, AC3 deliberately uses designer-user (spec line 95-97 states this explicitly) so no cross-test row collision; the new reset only touches AC3's own row, introducing no new pollution risk. (e) Self-sufficiency: each test performs its own token fetch and (for AC3) its own reset -- no test depends on another having run first; confirmed AC3 is now correct regardless of execution order or prior invocations, which is the entire point of this rework. (f) No hardcoded secrets beyond the same two already-vetted seeded dev credentials (admin-user/admin-pass, designer-user/designer-pass) -- grepped 'password|secret|pass' across the four files, every hit is one of those two credentials or the literal Keycloak protocol field name 'password' in form-encoding.

Re-verified AC4 myself, independently, this run: `docker compose ps` shows only the postgres service Up (Keycloak not running). Ran `mix test test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs` and got 'Excluding tags: [:keycloak]' / 'All tests have been excluded.' / 'Result: 0 tests, 3 excluded', quoted verbatim from this run's own terminal output. AC5's compliance ruling (raise-with-intended-message-text substituting for unsupported setup_all {:skip,_} return) stands from the prior gate iteration with no new contradicting evidence found this round.

git status --porcelain lib/ test/ is empty -- no stray files, no leftover mutant probes (none were needed or applied this round; this was a pre-fix code-reading verification, not a WF-03 pre-fix-nonexistence case, since the code under test already existed before this fix and the defect was a test-only baseline-acquisition bug, not a missing module).

gate_history.summary: AC1/AC2/AC6 pass; AC4 and AC5 independently re-verified and AC5's raise-vs-skip deviation ruled compliant. BLOCKER found under checks (c)/(d): AC3's test asserted a hardcoded pre-call count of 0 for designer-user's JIT-provisioned row, but the bpm-default tenant/schema (and any row provisioned in it) is never torn down between invocations (design section 5), and designer-user is a fixed seeded Keycloak identity with no per-run uniqueness available -- so the test passes on a database's first-ever run and fails deterministically on every subsequent run of AC6's own documented command.
issues: BLOCKER: AC3's hardcoded pre-call count of 0 is not repeatable across invocations of the same persistent test database; rework required via either (a) an on_exit/teardown deleting the JIT-provisioned row after the test, or (b) a count captured before either pipeline call as a baseline, asserted as count_before/count_before+1/count_before+1.
gate_history.next_action: Rework TEST-DESIGNER -- fix AC3's test repeatability defect, rework iteration 1 of 3.

gate_history.summary: AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5/AC6 re-confirmed passing (AC4 re-run: 'Excluding tags: [:keycloak]' / 'Result: 0 tests, 3 excluded' with Keycloak stopped). AC3's rework-1 fix (count_before baseline captured immediately before the first call, without resetting the row) does NOT eliminate the cross-invocation defect -- it moves it. Traced through lib/letflow/identity.ex's provision_oidc_user/4 -> upsert_by_external_identity/4 (genuine find-or-create keyed on tenant_id/external_realm/external_id): on a database's first-ever run count_before=0 and the sequence 0->1->1 holds, but on the second invocation of AC6's own documented command against the same never-torn-down bpm-default schema, designer-user's row from run 1 already exists, so count_before is captured as 1, call 1 correctly reuses the existing row (no insert), and `assert user_count_for_subject(...) == count_before + 1` fails deterministically because the post-call-1 count (1) equals count_before (1), not count_before+1 (2). Same failure class as iteration 0, just relocated to a later invocation and a different line.
issues: BLOCKER: test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs AC3 test (line 241-273 in that revision): count_before captured without first resetting live database state is not repeatable across invocations of AC6's documented command, because provision_oidc_user/4's find-or-create correctly reuses a row surviving from any prior invocation. Rework required: reset this subject's row to a true zero (e.g. Repo.delete_all scoped to external_realm/external_id in the tenant's schema) immediately after deriving `subject`, before computing any baseline. Reflect the corrected mechanism in test/specs/REQ-134.md's AC3 section.
gate_history.next_action: Rework TEST-DESIGNER -- fix AC3's still-unresolved cross-invocation repeatability defect (BLOCKER above), rework iteration 2 of 3. AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5/AC6 and checks (a)/(b)/(e) all PASS and do not need to be revisited; only the AC3 baseline-reset mechanism needs rework.
